fields.title: A build of kac takes whichever .NET 10 SDK the runner installs

sections.What we are doing instead:
Each job that built `kac` installed the SDK with [tol-setup-dotnet](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/8ea1b5a5f9f175b28a13b15fe1ccd03249bf34af/examples/dog-fooding/tools/workflows/setup-dotnet.md) and `dotnet-version: 10.0.x`, which took the newest 10.0 SDK on the day. [tol-dotnet-sdk](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/8ea1b5a5f9f175b28a13b15fe1ccd03249bf34af/examples/dog-fooding/tools/build/dotnet-sdk.md) approved the same range. No `global.json` fixed the version, so version control alone did not say which SDK built a commit.

The package published to nuget.org was built once, by the publish workflow, from the commit on `main`. Its run log showed the SDK that job installed.
sections.Why we need it: Fixing the version needed a `global.json` and a way to move it when a patch shipped, and neither had been set up. The range took each SDK patch without a pull request.
sections.What the risk is: Two builds of one commit could run on different SDK patches, and a difference between them showed only in the package that shipped. Nothing here would explain it without reading both run logs. An SDK patch seldom changes what a build produces, so the cost was a confusing difference and not a broken release.
sections.What compensates:
* The publish workflow was the only thing that built what shipped, and its run log recorded the commit and the SDK.
* [ctl-0007](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/8ea1b5a5f9f175b28a13b15fe1ccd03249bf34af/examples/dog-fooding/controls/0007-corpus-validation.md) packs the tool and installs it on every pull request. That copy runs `kac new` and validates the corpus
  it created, so a build that cannot run is caught before it ships.
* nuget.org never lets a published version be replaced, so a rebuild cannot overwrite what people already have.
sections.How it closes: [#971](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/issues/971) closed it. `global.json` at the repository root names the exact SDK with `rollForward: disable`. Every workflow installs the version it names with `global-json-file`, and Dependabot moves it when a patch ships. [tol-dotnet-sdk](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/8ea1b5a5f9f175b28a13b15fe1ccd03249bf34af/examples/dog-fooding/tools/build/dotnet-sdk.md) states the version.
sections.Scope: Every build of `kac`: the publish workflow, CI, and a contributor's own machine.
